section: Why Not Just Use PubMed Alerts?
text:
Why Not Just Use PubMed Alerts?
PubMed alerts are a reasonable starting point, but they have a key limitation: they give you a flat, unsorted list. If you set up an alert for “inflammatory bowel disease,” every matching paper arrives in the same inbox pile - therapeutics next to epidemiology next to basic science - and you still have to read through everything to find what’s relevant to your work.
IBD LitMonitor takes a different approach. Instead of delivering a raw feed, it organizes papers into sub-fields so you can go straight to the topic area you care about and skip the rest. Each category is collapsible, so browsing the day’s literature takes minutes rather than a lengthy inbox triage.

title: Design Decisions Log
text:
This file records durable product and operations decisions for IBD LitMonitor.
Last updated: 2026-04-17






Source repo: ibd-litmonitor-src (private).
Public repo: ibd-litmonitor (docs-only rendered output).

Why:

Keeps source internals private.
Keeps public history focused on published artifacts.
Makes GitHub Pages hosting straightforward.





Local work should be reset/synced to origin/main when uncertain.
Stale local edits/worktrees should be treated as disposable unless intentionally preserved.








Current cron: 30 12 * * *.
Notes:

This maps to 05:30 America/Los_Angeles at present.
Runtime uses TZ=America/Los_Angeles to align report dates with intended local date context.





Script treats all subscribers as weekly recipients.
Sends on Friday only.
Manual workflow triggers do not send digest.

Why:

Reduces noise/spam risk.
Keeps manual render/testing safe.









Added Intestinal Ultrasound (IUS).
Renamed existing imaging bucket to Endoscopy & Imaging (non-IUS).

Why:

IUS papers have distinct clinical workflow and should be discoverable separately.





Added Point of Care Testing (non-IUS).

Why:

Biosensor and POCT papers were being mixed into biomarker/imaging buckets.





data/overrides.csv is the durable human-reviewed correction layer.
Automated audit logic should not fight accepted override PMIDs.





data/exclusions.csv captures known non-IBD PMIDs permanently.









Category audit GH workflow was deleted.
Review is now human-in-the-loop and can be run with Codex routines.

Why:

Prevent noisy automated PR churn.
Keep final decisions centralized in review conversations and overrides.








Implementation:

Table data is pre-sorted by parsed date descending before DataTables initialization.
Interactive sorting/filtering remains available.

Reason:

Users opening dashboard should immediately see newest papers.





publication_date: original source display value.
publication_date_sort: normalized date key for reliable ordering.

Reason:

PubMed includes partial date formats.
Sorting requires normalized date parsing while preserving original display text.









Flagship if impact_factor >= 6.7 from data/journal_impact_factors.csv.
Plus curated fallback list in code for key GI journals.

Reason:

Makes policy objective and updateable.
Preserves expected highlighting for key journals with naming/lookup variance.









Replace fixed-number wording with count-agnostic phrasing.
Examples: sub-fields, topic groups, relevant research categories.

Reason:

Taxonomy evolves over time.
Hardcoded numbers become stale and misleading.





Use : style in features list (instead of em dashes) for consistency and readability.









Push source and public repos regularly.
Persist important decisions in repo docs, not only chat memory.
Back up $CODEX_HOME before major app updates.

Reason:

Reduces risk of local state loss or context fragmentation.







Keep manual-review authority over automated heuristics.
Prefer conservative rule changes; use overrides for one-offs.
Treat user-facing copy as taxonomy-agnostic unless numbers are dynamically computed.
Keep deployment path simple and observable.

NoteHow to Read This Report



Coverage: PubMed queries across a broad set of IBD topic groups, deduplicated - each paper appears exactly once in the most specific matching category.
Categorisation: Automatic and imperfect - a paper found by multiple queries is assigned to the most specific one (e.g. a vedolizumab trial in children goes to Pediatric IBD). For keyword search across all categories or papers from the past 30 days, use the Interactive Dashboard.
Study design badges RCT Meta-analysis Review are shown only when PubMed has explicitly assigned a publication type. Papers published within the last 1-2 weeks often don’t have a badge yet.
★ Flagship journals: Papers from Gut, Gastroenterology, Lancet, NEJM, JCC, and other leading GI journals are marked ★.
Spotted something wrong or have a suggestion?  Send feedback →

Subcutaneous infliximab in inflammatory bowel disease: from pharmacokinetic principles to clinical practice.Review  Expert opinion on biological therapy  |  2026-10-09



Subcutaneous infliximab (CT-P13 SC) was developed to address the pronounced peak-to-trough fluctuations of intravenous dosing and the immunogenicity driven by sub-therapeutic troughs. Through a stable steady-state pharmacokinetic profile it meets the international Delphi consensus definition of a biobetter, although this is not a regulatory designation. This narrative review synthesizes pivotal Phase 3 trial data, randomized comparisons of continued intravenous versus subcutaneous maintenance, real-world switching cohorts, individual participant data meta-analyses, and emerging evidence on therapeutic drug monitoring recalibration, immunomodulator de-escalation, and special populations including obesity, perianal disease, pediatric inflammatory bowel disease, and pregnancy. MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to August 2026. Subcutaneous infliximab is positioned to become the default maintenance route for most patients, with intravenous administration reserved for acute, high-burden induction. Within five years, fully subcutaneous pathways, immunomodulator de-escalation guided by steady-state levels, and dosing informed by individual clearance are expected to move from research questions to standard practice.


Quraishi MN, El Ouali S

Differential long-term efficacy of biologic and small-molecule therapies by disease location in moderate-to-severe luminal Crohn’s disease: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.★  Inflammatory bowel diseases  |  2026-10-08



Treatment efficacy in Crohn’s disease (CD) may vary according to disease location. We aimed to evaluate the long-term efficacy of biological and small molecule therapies in moderate-to-severe luminal CD stratified by CD location. We conducted a systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis (NMA) of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) in adults (aged ≥18 years) with moderate-to-severe CD (Crohn’s Disease Activity Index [CDAI] 220-450), identified through PubMed, Embase, and CENTRAL to August 12, 2025. Predefined outcomes included clinical remission (CDAI < 150) and endoscopic response (≥50% reduction in Simple Endoscopic Score-CD (SES-CD) at week 52 (range, 44-56 weeks), stratified by Montreal disease location and trial design. Eighteen RCTs (including 4697 patients) evaluating adalimumab, infliximab, vedolizumab, ustekinumab, mirikizumab, risankizumab, guselkumab, and upadacitinib were included. Clinical remission rates were lowest in isolated ileal disease, and only guselkumab regimens (200 mg/100 mg: relative risk, 3.4 [95% CI, 1.3-8.9]) were statistically superior to placebo for maintenance of clinical remission at week 52. In isolated colonic disease, upadacitinib 30 mg ranked highest in re-randomized trials and with significant location-dependent differences (efficacy ratio [EF] for colonic vs ileal is 4.6 [95% CI, 1.7-12.6], EF for ileocolonic vs ileal is 3.45 [95% CI, 1.2-9.6]), consistent with endoscopic response rates. No location-dependent differences were observed for other agents. Relative efficacy of advanced therapies in luminal CD varied by disease location. These findings support consideration of disease location in personalized treatment decision-making to improve clinical outcomes.


Dalsgarð SP, Pkb KKB, Seidelin JB, Bjerrum JT, Attauabi M


DOI: 10.1093/ibd/izag177  |  View on PubMed →





Hospitalized Infection Risk and Organ-specific Infection Patterns Across Advanced Therapies in Ulcerative Colitis: A Japanese Claims Analysis.  Internal medicine (Tokyo, Japan)  |  2026-10-08



Background Evidence comparing infections across advanced therapies (ADTs) for ulcerative colitis (UC) remains inconsistent, and infection category profiles are poorly characterized, particularly in real-world Japanese settings. We compared the risk of hospitalized infections and descriptively characterized the distribution of infection categories among hospitalized infection events across ADTs.Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Medical Data Vision Database. Patients with UC who initiated treatment with a tumor necrosis factor (TNF) antagonist, ustekinumab, tofacitinib, or vedolizumab between April 2008 and May 2022 were followed. Adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) were estimated using Cox models (TNF antagonists as the reference), and hospitalized infections were classified according to the organ system.Results We included 9,012 patients receiving ADTs (TNF antagonists, 3,990; ustekinumab, 1,380; tofacitinib, 1,183; and vedolizumab, 2,459). Hospitalized infections occurred in 90, 16, 21, and 52 patients prescribed TNF antagonists, ustekinumab, tofacitinib, and vedolizumab, respectively; the incidence rates per 1,000 person-years were 19.09, 9.64, 14.53, and 17.24, respectively. In the multivariable analysis, ustekinumab was associated with a lower risk of hospitalized infection than TNF antagonists (aHR 0.46, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.25-0.82), whereas tofacitinib (aHR 0.73, 95% CI 0.43-1.22) and vedolizumab (aHR 0.76, 95% CI 0.53-1.10) were not significantly different. Among the first hospitalized infection events, the distribution of infection categories was comparable across ADTs, with respiratory infections being the most common.Conclusions Ustekinumab was associated with a lower risk of infection-related hospitalization than TNF antagonists. The distribution of infection categories among the first hospitalized infection events was comparable across the ADTs. These findings provide the first large-scale, real-world, comparative evidence from Japan.


Nishida Y, Hosomi S, Nakata R, Maruyama H, Ominami M, Nadatani Y, Fukunaga S, Otani K, Fujiwara Y


DOI: 10.2169/internalmedicine.7882-26  |  View on PubMed →





Longitudinal SARS-CoV-2 mRNA vaccine immunogenicity in inflammatory bowel disease in relation to anti-TNF therapy and age: a prospective cohort study.  Vaccine  |  2026-10-08



Patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) on immunomodulatory therapy may respond less well to vaccination. We followed humoral and cellular responses to SARS-CoV-2 vaccination over 12 months. In this single-centre, prospective cohort study, adults with IBD received mRNA vaccine under the Austrian national programme. Two doses were administered 28 days apart and a third dose 6-12 months after the first. S1-RBD IgG, live-virus 50% neutralisation titres (NT50) against wild-type, Delta, Omicron BA.1 and BA.2, and IFN-γ ELISpot responses were measured at baseline and after 3, 6 and 12 months. Associations with anti-TNF therapy and age were analysed with rank-based longitudinal models and with mixed-effects models adjusted for age and sex. All 53 twice-vaccinated, infection-naive patients seroconverted at 3 months. Geometric mean (GM) S1-RBD IgG peaked at 3 months (465.7 BAU/ml) and fell by 6 months (124.8 BAU/ml). At 3 months, GM NT50 values were lower against BA.1 (9.0) than against wild-type (24.2) or Delta (26.9), and 13 patients (24.5%) never reached a wild-type NT50 of 1:16. Anti-TNF therapy (32/53, 60.4%) was significantly associated with faster waning. At 6 months, adjusted geometric mean ratio versus other therapy was 0.31 (95% CI 0.20-0.49) for S1-RBD IgG and 0.22 (0.12-0.41) for wild-type NT50. Each additional year of age was associated with 2.4% lower wild-type NT50 (0.976 per year, 95% CI 0.962-0.990). In 33 thrice-vaccinated patients, intercurrent infection (15/33) raised S1-RBD IgG 4.6-fold more than the third dose alone, without a measurable gain in neutralisation. In the adjusted model, IFN-γ ELISpot responses did not differ between treatment groups. Anti-TNF therapy and higher age within a relatively young cohort were associated with lower and shorter-lived humoral responses, while cellular responses appeared comparatively preserved. These exploratory associations need confirmation in larger cohorts with clinical endpoints.


Mayr W, Knell AI, Boehm AK, Jäger M, Ennemoser L, Griesmacher A, Bellmann-Weiler R, Koch R, Tilg H, Posch W


DOI: 10.1016/j.vaccine.2026.129224  |  View on PubMed →





EVOLVE-IBERIA: Real-world evidence on vedolizumab and anti-tumour necrosis factor-α as first- and second-line biologic treatment in Crohn’s disease.  Gastroenterologia y hepatologia  |  2026-10-07



Much of the available real-world evidence on the gut-selective α4β7 integrin antibody vedolizumab comes from patients with repeated failure of anti-tumour necrosis factor-α (anti-TNFα) agents and other treatments. The EVOLVE-IBERIA study is aimed to generate additional real-world evidence for vedolizumab and anti-as first- or second-line biologic treatment, in patients with Crohn’s disease or ulcerative colitis; here we present the outcomes in patients with Crohn’s disease. Medical charts of patients aged 18 years or older treated with vedolizumab or anti-TNFα as first- or second-line biologic in Spain and Portugal were retrospectively reviewed; both cohorts therefore included biologic-naive and biologic-exposed patients to compare the clinical effectiveness, safety and treatment patterns of vedolizumab and anti, and to characterize healthcare resource utilisation. Analyses were adjusted by means of propensity scores using inverse probability of treatment weighting. A total of 210 patients with Crohn’s disease were included; median follow-up was 26.0 months. At Week 52, clinical response rates were 74.8% and 69.8% (p=0.481) and clinical remission rates were 51.3% and 66.5% (p=0.065), in the vedolizumab cohort and in the anti-TNFα cohort, respectively. Treatment-related adverse event rates per 100 patient-years were 1.15 in the vedolizumab cohort and 2.70 in the anti-TNFαcohort (p=0.024). In the real-world setting, the comparable long-term effectiveness and lower incidence of treatment-related adverse events of vedolizumab compared with anti-suggest a favourable benefit: risk ratio of vedolizumab as first- or second-line biologic treatment in patients with Crohn’s disease.

Multi-omics and machine learning identify neutrophil annexin A3 as a therapeutic target of ginsenoside Rb1 for comorbidity of ischaemic stroke and ulcerative colitis.★  British journal of pharmacology  |  2026-10-07



Epidemiological evidence suggests a bidirectional relationship between ischaemic stroke (IS) and ulcerative colitis (UC), yet the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. Four IS and three UC datasets from the gene expression omnibus (GEO) database were analysed to identify key comorbidity genes. Two-sample Mendelian randomisation (MR) was conducted to infer causal relationships. Clinical validations utilised peripheral blood neutrophils from UC-IS patients, assessed via western blotting and quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR). The direct binding of ginsenoside Rb1 to annexin A3 (ANXA3) was verified through molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations and cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA). MR analysis indicated a causal association between ANXA3 expression and increased risk of IS and UC. Immune infiltration analysis demonstrated a strong positive correlation between ANXA3 expression and neutrophil infiltration in both IS and UC. ScRNA-seq confirmed that ANXA3 was expressed in neutrophils within diseased tissues. Circulating neutrophils from UC-IS comorbidity patients showed significantly elevated ANXA3 mRNA and protein levels. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed a stable ginsenoside Rb1-ANXA3 complex with favourable binding free energy. CETSA confirmed the direct binding of ginsenoside Rb1 to ANXA3 in primary human neutrophils. UC-IS serum induced neutrophil hyperactivation, including excessive migration, NETosis, myeloperoxidase (MPO) release and reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, which was significantly attenuated by ginsenoside Rb1 in vitro. ANXA3 is a predominant neutrophil-derived biomarker linking UC-IS comorbidity. Ginsenoside Rb1 mitigates comorbidity-induced neutrophil hyperactivation by directly binding ANXA3, representing a promising therapeutic strategy.


Zhou J, Li P, Yu E, Chen J, Zhou M, Li Y, Hu J, Guo S, Hu H, Yuan Y

Upadacitinib and upadacitinib-vedolizumab combination therapy for refractory pediatric-onset inflammatory bowel disease.  Intestinal research  |  2026-10-06



To evaluate the efficacy and safety of upadacitinib in patients with highly refractory pediatric-onset inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and to describe the outcomes of upadacitinib-vedolizumab combination therapy (UVCT) in treatment-refractory cases. This retrospective, single-center study included 18 patients (7 with ulcerative colitis, 6 with Crohn’s disease, and 5 with very early-onset IBD) who received upadacitinib between November 2022 and November 2025. Five patients underwent UVCT. All patients had previously failed multiple therapies (median, 3 prior advanced therapies). The primary outcome was the upadacitinib continuation rate. The secondary outcomes included corticosteroid- and tacrolimusfree remission rates, safety profiles, and UVCT outcomes. The median age at upadacitinib initiation was 13.0 years (range, 2.3-21.6 years). The 52-week continuation rate was 55.6%. Among patients who received corticosteroids at baseline, 50% achieved corticosteroid-free status by 6 months; all patients who received tacrolimus at baseline discontinued tacrolimus within 6 months. No serious adverse events attributable to upadacitinib were observed and no cases of herpes zoster reactivation occurred. Five patients with persistent corticosteroid/tacrolimus dependence underwent UVCT, 4 of whom achieved clinical remission with withdrawal of corticosteroids/tacrolimus, with endoscopic improvement confirmed in 3. One patient with very early-onset IBD required colectomy. Upadacitinib demonstrated acceptable efficacy and safety in patients with highly refractory pediatric-onset IBD. In this small subgroup, UVCT was associated with clinical remission in most patients (4/5), suggesting that it may warrant further investigation as a salvage strategy to avert surgery. Prospective, multicenter studies are needed to define the optimal positioning within pediatric-onset IBD treatment algorithms.


Shimizu H, Takeuchi I, Oue H, To H, Tanioka A, Komorizono R, Arai K

EFFICACY AND SAFETY OF ADVANCED THERAPIES AS INDUCTION THERAPY FOR ULCERATIVE COLITIS: AN UPDATED SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND NETWORK META-ANALYSIS.Review★  Clinical gastroenterology and hepatology : the official clinical practice journal of the American Gastroenterological Association  |  2026-10-06



Advanced therapies (ATs) are central to the management of moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis (UC). The expanding therapeutic landscape and limited head-to-head trials necessitate updated comparative effectiveness analyses. We performed a systematic review and network meta-analysis (NMA) to assess the efficacy and safety of ATs as induction therapy for UC. We searched MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane CENTRAL. We included phase 3 randomized controlled trials evaluating approved ATs or agents in late-stage development for induction therapy in moderate-to-severe UC. Pairwise meta-analyses and NMA were conducted using a frequentist random-effects model. Confidence was evaluated using the CINeMA framework. The primary outcome was clinical remission; secondary outcomes included endoscopic improvement, serious adverse events (SAEs), adverse events leading to discontinuation (AELDs), and serious infections. Analyses were stratified by prior exposure to ATs. Thirty-three induction trials involving 17 therapies, were included. Upadacitinib demonstrated the highest relative efficacy for clinical remission (RR 6.90; 95% CI 3.54-12.45; P-score 0.95; high confidence) and endoscopic improvement (RR 5.29; 95% CI 3.38-8.28; P-score 0.97; moderate confidence). In AT-naïve patients, obefazimod and upadacitinib showed the highest efficacy, whereas in AT-experienced patients, upadacitinib, ustekinumab, and tofacitinib ranked highest. Anti-p19 inhibitors, including risankizumab, subcutaneous guselkumab, and mirikizumab, were associated with the most favorable safety profiles for SAEs and AELDs, although confidence in safety estimates was lower. Upadacitinib has high efficacy for induction of clinical remission and endoscopic improvement in AT-naïve and AT-experienced patients. Novel therapies, like obefazimod and guselkumab subcutaneous, may represent highly effective alternatives. Anti-p19 inhibitors offer a favorable safety profile.


Olivera PA, Lasa JS, Singh S, Jairath V, Fumery M, Sands BE, Danese S, Peyrin-Biroulet L


DOI: 10.1016/j.cgh.2026.09.038  |  View on PubMed →





Janus Kinase Inhibitors for Acute Severe Ulcerative Colitis: Comparing Upadacitinib to Tofacitinib and Rescue to Sequential Salvage therapy.★  Clinical gastroenterology and hepatology : the official clinical practice journal of the American Gastroenterological Association  |  2026-10-06



Acute Severe Ulcerative Colitis (ASUC) remains a medical emergency with limited therapeutic options. Upadacitinib and tofacitinib are Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitors being increasingly used as rescue therapy for ASUC with limited data. We evaluated outcomes of JAK inhibitor use for ASUC over 52 weeks. We undertook a multicentre retrospective cohort study across 13 Australian IBD centres. Adults with ASUC who commenced upadacitinib or tofacitinib from April 2021 to April 2024 were included. Outcomes were assessed during index admission, at week 8, 16, and 52. Comparisons of upadacitinib vs tofacitinib and rescue vs sequential salvage therapy were undertaken. The primary outcome for both analyses was colectomy by week 52. 150 patients were included with complete follow-up to 52 weeks. Upadacitinib was used in 51%, tofacitinib in 49%; JAK inhibitors as rescue therapy in 69% and sequential salvage therapy in 31%. Colectomy occurred in 33% of patients by week 52, and was significantly lower with upadacitinib than tofacitinib (23.4% vs 42.5%, weighted marginal risk difference -0.18, p=0.022), with no significance at earlier timepoints. Sequential salvage therapy resulted in a numerically higher rate of colectomy compared to Rescue therapy (38% vs 30%, adjusted marginal risk difference -0.1, p=0.239), but did not meet statistical significance. JAK inhibitors were effective for ASUC with a reassuring safety profile. Upadacitinib use resulted in a significantly lower rate of colectomy by week 52, with higher rates of clinical remission, CFCR, and biochemical remission during follow-up. Sequential salvage therapy may represent a viable therapeutic option for patients otherwise facing colectomy.


Gilmore R, Fernandes R, Goetz N, Chin S, Con D, De Cruz P, Demase K, Sparrow MP, Lucas S, Garg M


DOI: 10.1016/j.cgh.2026.10.001  |  View on PubMed →





Investigation of the protective effect of adalimumab on stricture and inflammation in an experimental corrosive esophageal burn model in rats.  Cirugia y cirujanos  |  2026-10-06



This study aimed to investigate the effectiveness of the tumor necrosis factor-α inhibitor adalimumab on inflammation and subsequent stricture development in a corrosive esophageal burn model in rats, based on its antifibrotic effect in Crohn’s disease. Forty-eight female Wistar Albino rats were randomized into four groups (n = 12): control, local intraluminal adalimumab (5 mg/kg), systemic subcutaneous adalimumab (5 mg/kg), and combined local plus systemic adalimumab. A corrosive esophageal burn was created in all animals. After 10 days, the distal esophageal segment was excised and evaluated by stenosis index (SI), histopathologic damage score (HDS), and tissue hydroxyproline level. Data were analyzed using non-parametric tests. Compared with the control group, the systemic and combined groups showed a significant reduction in SI and hydroxyproline level (p < 0.05). The combined group also reduced HDS. Local adalimumab showed no difference from the control. Systemic adalimumab reduced inflammation and stenosis in corrosive esophageal burns, whereas local administration had no significant effect. Further clinical studies are needed before adalimumab can be considered for these injuries. Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is increasingly recognized as a systemic disorder involving gut-brain axis dysfunction and neuropsychiatric comorbidities, yet safe and mechanistically defined neuromodulatory strategies remain limited. This study aimed to investigate whether non-invasive spleen-targeted ultrasound regulates gut-brain communication through peripheral neuroimmune signaling in colitis. Male C57BL/6J mice with dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced acute colitis were treated with focused ultrasound stimulation of the spleen (sFUS) at intensities of 0.5 or 1.0 W/cm2. Subdiaphragmatic vagotomy (SDV) or sham surgery was performed before DSS induction and subsequent sFUS treatment to examine the involvement of vagal signaling. Therapeutic outcomes were evaluated using histological, molecular, microbiome, transcriptomic, and behavioral analyses. sFUS attenuated intestinal and neuroinflammation by reducing the mRNA levels of the pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α, together with modulation of splenic cholinergic signaling and attenuation of systemic inflammatory responses. Furthermore, sFUS restored intestinal barrier integrity by increasing the expression of the tight junction proteins ZO-1 and Occludin, with significant restoration of ZO-1 only at 0.5 W/cm2, ameliorating histopathological damage and re-establishing gut microbiota homeostasis. These protective effects were associated with improvements in anxiety-like behavior and cognitive performance. Importantly, the therapeutic benefits of sFUS were abolished by SDV, demonstrating their dependence on intact vagal signaling, and were accompanied by activation of the nucleus tractus solitarius-locus coeruleus circuit and adrenergic-cAMP-MAPK-CREB/BDNF signaling in the prefrontal cortex. Crohn’s disease (CD) frequently progresses to stricturing or penetrating behavior, which often necessitates surgical or interventional management. Accurate, real-time assessment of these complications is essential for optimizing therapeutic strategies. This review summarizes the current evidence on the utility of intestinal ultrasound (IUS) and its advanced modalities in diagnosing, characterizing, and monitoring complicated CD. As a noninvasive, radiation-free, and cost-effective point-of-care tool, IUS demonstrates high diagnostic accuracy for detecting intestinal strictures, comparable to computed tomography and magnetic resonance enterography, and its diagnostic performance can be further enhanced by the use of small intestine contrast ultrasonography (SICUS). Furthermore, IUS exhibits strong diagnostic performance in detecting penetrating complications, including abscess and fistulas. The diagnostic yield for these lesions is significantly enhanced by SICUS, which utilizes luminal distension to better visualize extra-luminal tracts. Notably, CEUS plays an important role in distinguishing true avascular abscesses from phlegmons. In conclusion, IUS has established itself as a highly reliable imaging modality for the evaluation of complicated CD. The primary outcome was the proportion of process indicators followed by speciality per pregnancy. Forty-three pregnancies amongst 43 individuals were included; 19 (44.2%) had ulcerative colitis. Biologics improve outcomes in inflammatory bowel disease, but high costs restrict access and strain healthcare resources. Biosimilars lower costs, expand access, and support sustainable IBD care. Provide clear, evidence-based answers on biosimilar use in IBD across clinical, therapeutic, and economic domains to guide safe implementation and informed decision-making. GEDIIB conducted a PICO-structured systematic review across multiple databases and trial registries. We extracted clinically relevant outcomes and performed systematic review. We assessed risk of bias with RoB 2.0 and ROBINS-I and graded certainty using GRADE. A structured Delphi process with two voting rounds and external validation finalized recommendations, with consensus predefined at 85 percent or higher. Anti-TNF biosimilars and originator biologics have similar efficacy, safety, immunogenicity, treatment persistence, and mucosal healing in biologic-naive patients and after switching, with no clinically meaningful differences in adverse events, loss of response, or discontinuation. Data on multiple switches do not indicate harm, though evidence remains limited. Pediatric studies suggest similar profiles, with lower precision. Economic evaluations show substantial cost savings and improved access, supporting the sustainability of the health system. Biosimilars represent a viable, safe, and cost-effective option for IBD management. We recommend structured switching strategies, clear communication with patients, and continuous clinical monitoring. Additional robust studies should strengthen evidence in specific populations and clinical scenarios. Os medicamentos biológicos melhoraram significativamente os desfechos clínicos na doença inflamatória intestinal (DII); entretanto, seus elevados custos limitam o acesso ao tratamento e impõem um impacto considerável aos sistemas de saúde. Os biossimilares reduzem custos, ampliam o acesso aos tratamentos e contribuem para a sustentabilidade da assistência aos pacientes com DII. Fornecer respostas claras e baseadas em evidências sobre o uso de biossimilares na DII, abrangendo aspectos clínicos, terapêuticos e econômicos, a fim de orientar sua implementação segura e subsidiar a tomada de decisões informadas. Foram extraídos desfechos clinicamente relevantes e realizada uma revisão sistemática. O risco de viés foi avaliado por meio das ferramentas RoB 2.0 e ROBINS-I, e a certeza da evidência foi classificada utilizando a metodologia GRADE. As recomendações foram elaboradas e validadas por meio de um processo Delphi estruturado, composto por duas rodadas de votação e de validação externa, tendo como consenso a concordância igual ou superior a 85%. A high-fat diet (HFD) is closely associated with the progression of ulcerative colitis (UC). However, the underlying mechanisms, particularly the interplay among lipid metabolic disturbances, mitochondrial damage, and intestinal barrier dysfunction, remain poorly defined. This study aimed to elucidate the molecular mechanisms by which HFD exacerbates DSS-induced UC, with a focus on the role of the AMPK/PPARα axis in mediating lipotoxicity and mitochondrial dysfunction that promote UC progression. A murine UC model was established in C57BL/6 mice by HFD feeding combined with DSS administration, along with an in vitro co-stimulation system using Caco-2 cells exposed to palmitic acid (PA) and lipopolysaccharide (LPS). Pathological phenotypes and molecular pathway alterations were systematically evaluated by hematoxylin and eosin (HE) staining, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), molecular biological techniques, and intervention with the specific AMPK agonist AICAR. HFD significantly exacerbated DSS-induced colitis, as manifested by rapid weight loss, elevated disease activity index, and destruction of mucosal tissue architecture. Mechanistically, HFD led to intestinal epithelial lipid accumulation and gut microbiota dysbiosis, which synergistically triggered oxidative stress and paradoxically suppressed AMPK phosphorylation (p-AMPK). AMPK inactivation downregulates PPARα and its downstream fatty acid oxidation enzymes (CPT1A and ACOX1), exacerbating lipotoxicity and mitochondrial ultrastructural damage. Concurrently, decreased expression of key respiratory chain subunits (NDUFS2 and MTCO2) ultimately culminates in an energy crisis. Notably, pharmacological activation of AMPK using AICAR effectively reversed p-AMPK inhibition, restored PPARα expression, and ameliorated intestinal barrier function, demonstrating that the AMPK pathway serves as a critical pathogenic driver. HFD, through lipotoxicity and microbiota-derived pro-inflammatory signals, induces paradoxical inactivation of the intestinal epithelial AMPK/PPARα axis, which subsequently blocks fatty acid oxidation, provokes mitochondrial dysfunction and ATP depletion, and ultimately leads to breakdown of the intestinal barrier. This study uncovers a novel mechanistic link among metabolism, mitochondrial function, and gut barrier integrity, providing a solid theoretical and experimental foundation for precision metabolic reprogramming-based therapies in UC patients with metabolic derangements.

However, the Controlling Nutritional Status (CONUT) score is a simple tool based on laboratory analysis; its performance in early malnutrition detection could be improved. Our aim was to exploratorily derive and assess the apparent diagnostic performance of enhanced CONUT-based scores (eCONUT-UC) for identifying GLIM-defined malnutrition in patients with ulcerative colitis. We conducted a cross-sectional study in patients with ulcerative colitis. We measured weight, height, body mass index, and body composition using DXA and BIA. We extracted recent laboratory results and clinical data from medical records. We used the GLIM criteria as the reference standard for detecting malnutrition in ulcerative colitis. We evaluated the diagnostic performance of the eCONUT-UC by incorporating phase angle (PhA), hemoglobin (Hgb), and triglycerides (TG). We calculated sensitivity, specificity, and area under the curve (AUC). We included 51 patients, of whom 15 (29%) met GLIM criteria for malnutrition. The original CONUT score had a sensitivity of 73% and a specificity of 67%. The eCONUT-UC-PhA and eCONUT-UC-Hgb showed a sensitivity of 80%, with an AUC of 0.741 [95% CI: 0.587-0.895] and 0.738 [95% CI: 0.586-0.890]. The eCONUT-UC-TG showed lower diagnostic performance. Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic inflammatory bowel disease with a complex and incompletely understood pathogenesis. This study aimed to prioritize candidate genes associated with UC and characterize their potential genetic and immune-related molecular context using an integrative transcriptomic and genetic framework. Bulk transcriptomic analysis was first performed using the discovery cohort GSE87466. After duplicated gene symbols were collapsed by mean expression, differential expression analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) were conducted to identify UC-related candidate genes. Candidate genes for downstream analyses were defined by the overlap between differentially expressed genes and genes within selected WGCNA core modules. An expression quantitative trait locus-based summary-data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR) framework integrating UC genome-wide association study data with blood-derived eQTL data was subsequently applied to prioritize putative gene-disease associations. Functional enrichment analysis, CIBERSORT-based immune infiltration analysis, single-gene gene set enrichment analysis, and single-cell RNA sequencing analyses were performed to characterize the biological context of the prioritized genes. Three independent transcriptomic cohorts were used for external validation, and a small DSS-induced colitis mouse experiment was used for exploratory experimental assessment. eQTL-based SMR analysis identified IRF1 and JAK2 as candidate genes associated with UC susceptibility. IRF1 was prioritized for downstream characterization based on convergent evidence from transcriptomic, immune, single-cell, and experimental analyses. IRF1 expression was associated with multiple CIBERSORT-inferred immune-cell proportions, including positive correlations with M1 macrophages, neutrophils, activated dendritic cells, and T follicular helper cells, and negative correlations with M2 macrophages and activated natural killer cells. Higher IRF1 expression was associated with interferon, NF-κB, and IL-6/JAK/STAT3 signaling pathways. Single-cell analysis showed IRF1 expression across myeloid cells, fibroblasts, endothelial cells, and epithelial cells. DSS-treated mice showed descriptively higher colonic IRF1 protein expression, providing preliminary experimental support consistent with human transcriptomic findings. IRF1 was prioritized as a candidate gene associated with UC and was linked to interferon-related inflammatory pathways and altered immune-cell profiles. These findings provide an integrated framework for further investigation of the potential role of IRF1 in UC. Given the use of blood-derived eQTL data and preliminary animal evidence, the findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and require further functional validation.
